title: Adjectives: Agreement
subtitle: Masculine and feminine, singular and plural. bon/bonne/bons/bonnes. Position: most adjectives follow the noun; a handful precede.
objectives: Form the feminine of regular adjectives by adding -e.
Form the plural of adjectives by adding -s.
Recognize irregular feminine and plural forms.
Apply correct adjective position: most follow the noun, a few precede.

sections.heading: Adjective agreement
sections.body:
French adjectives agree with the noun they modify in gender (masculine/feminine) and number (singular/plural).

Masculine singular → Feminine singular: add -e
  petit → petite (small)
  grand → grande (big)

If the masculine form already ends in -e, no change:
  jeune → jeune (young)

Singular → Plural: add -s
  petit → petits
  petite → petites

Complete paradigm for 'bon' (good):
  Masculine singular: bon
  Feminine singular: bonne
  Masculine plural: bons
  Feminine plural: bonnes

sections.heading: Irregular feminines
sections.body:
Some adjectives have irregular feminine forms.

  -eux → -euse: heureux → heureuse (happy)
  -er → -ère: cher → chère (dear, expensive)
  -f → -ve: actif → active (active)
  -on, -en → double consonant + e: bon → bonne, ancien → ancienne

These patterns are common. Learn them by seeing them in context.

sections.heading: Adjective position
sections.body:
Most French adjectives follow the noun:

  un livre intéressant (an interesting book)
  une maison blanche (a white house)

A small set of common adjectives precede the noun. The mnemonic is BAGS: Beauty, Age, Goodness, Size.

  Beauty: beau, joli (beautiful, pretty)
  Age: jeune, vieux, nouveau (young, old, new)
  Goodness: bon, mauvais (good, bad)
  Size: petit, grand, gros (small, big, large)

Examples:
  un petit garçon (a small boy)
  une belle maison (a beautiful house)
  un vieux livre (an old book)

Some adjectives change meaning depending on position:
  un homme grand (a tall man) vs. un grand homme (a great man)
  une voiture chère (an expensive car) vs. une chère amie (a dear friend)

sections.heading: Practice from Racine
sections.body:
From Phèdre, Act I:

  Noble et brillant auteur d'une triste famille
  (Noble and brilliant author of a sad family)

Here 'noble', 'brillant', and 'triste' all modify nouns. 'Triste' precedes 'famille' for emphasis, though it could follow.

items.prompt: Does 'petit' come before or after the noun?
items.answer: Before. It is a BAGS adjective (Size).

items.prompt: Does 'intéressant' come before or after the noun?
items.answer: After. Most adjectives follow the noun.
